labels.wrongElement: the prompt does not say whether the person is addressed with tú or usted; the closed key accepts only «¿Cómo te llamas?» and would mark «¿Cómo se llama?» / «¿Cómo se llama usted?» incorrect
labels.expectedFinding: Spanish has distinct singular forms of address (tú, usted; vos elsewhere); the Ukrainian prompt «в людини» fixes neither.

labels.wrongElement: key and rule hint require the possessive with a body part: option b «Me duele mi cabeza.» marked correct, option a «Me duele la cabeza.» marked incorrect, hint "…вживаємо присвійний займенник…"
labels.expectedFinding: With body parts the established use is the definite article (me duele la cabeza), not the possessive (me duele mi cabeza).
«ordenador» is the form used in Spain (computadora/computador are correct elsewhere).

labels.wrongElement: error variant "¿A dónde vas?" marked incorrect with feedback claiming the word must be written as one word
labels.expectedFinding: Interrogative adónde and a dónde are both accepted spellings with the same meaning.

labels.wrongElement: option b "Усі" is marked correct and option a "Ніхто" incorrect, contradicting the transcript «no viene nadie»
labels.expectedFinding: «No viene nadie» has the same meaning as «Nadie viene»: nobody comes; the negative word after the verb with no before it is the normal pattern, not a double positive.
After con the pronouns mí and ti take the forms conmigo and contigo.

labels.wrongElement: accepted key "veintiún" and error variant "veintiuna" marked incorrect before the feminine noun «personas»
labels.expectedFinding: Numerals ending in un/una agree in gender with the following noun: veintiuna personas, treinta y una personas — not «veintiún/treinta y un personas».

labels.wrongElement: error variant feedbackUk "Над останньою «e» потрібен апостроф…": «апостроф» names the Ukrainian apostrophe (’), not the written accent mark
labels.expectedFinding: In Ukrainian «апостроф» is the comma-shaped sign written after a consonant (п'ять); the acute mark is «знак наголосу» (акут), so the feedback names the wrong sign.
«акут» is a standard Ukrainian name for the acute sign (СУМ: знак цього наголосу на письмі), so «знак наголосу (акут)» is correct; también is written with the accent.
Existential haber stays singular in compound tenses too: ha habido problemas, not «han habido».

labels.wrongElement: «a las siete» has no de la mañana/de la tarde and no other context; the key accepts only "О 19:00" and marks "О 7:00" incorrect
labels.expectedFinding: In the 12-hour model the part of the day is given by de la mañana/tarde/noche; without it «a las siete» can be 7:00 or 19:00, and a class at either time is plausible.

labels.wrongElement: «La veo» refers to «una de ellas», the neighbour who works at the hospital, but the text never says whether that is Laura or Carmen; the key accepts only "Лауру"
labels.expectedFinding: la is the feminine singular direct-object pronoun; here it picks up «una de ellas», whose identity the text does not give.
